human.problem: The joke, 'Hidden in the dark for days, waiting on somebody to remember you're there… I have NO idea what that's like,' compares the loincloth to Papa Dorin's forgotten years in the drawer. This suggests the loincloth was forgotten. The text shows the opposite: the LORD planned to send Jeremiah back for 'the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there' (Jeremiah 13:6). The Reverence rules say humor never targets God. The Retelling rule says he never says anything the text shows is wrong, but it also says he may exaggerate in his own jokes. The docs don't say whether a joke that turns a deliberate act of God into a 'forgotten' one crosses either line.
human.question: Can Papa Dorin make a drawer joke that frames something God set aside on purpose as forgotten, when the 'somebody' doing the remembering is the LORD? Or should these drawer comparisons avoid suggesting God forgot?
